content.text:
Enriquez Saltillo explains that attacks on Starbottle and Richards were caused not by a ghostly Friar Pedro but by Cota’s trained, bullet-killed pinto horse. Grey returns to the Clarion office and abandons the story.

In “A Jack and Jill of the Sierras,” miner Edward Bray rescues Eugenia Neworth from a mountain ledge and escorts her along the perilous trail. Her note, “Think of Jill,” leads to a quartz discovery and romance.

In “Bilson’s Housekeeper,” practical Euphemia Trotter manages the Summit House. Chris Calton pretends to love Frida to win Euphemia’s attention, eventually confesses his love, and departs for San Francisco. Frida marries Bilson.

Frank Merriwell and Barney are captured by Black Caps in Tennessee, nearly hanged, and saved by Muriel—secretly Kate Kenyon. Kate leads them through an underground passage to an old mill, where they meet her escaped brother Rufe. Muriel later rescues them from Wade Miller, who is captured. The remaining articles discuss fruit processing, grape bags, solar heat, surveying a true meridian, an ocellated pheasant, the maidenhair tree, and American woods.
